title: Scrim: prefetch + batching field diary (week of 2027-09-06)
content:
Purpose
A short, informal week-diary capturing prefetch/prefill and batching experiments we ran in the scrim cluster, notes from standups, and action items for follow-up. This is intentionally lightweight — for recording what worked, what didn't, and open questions we can triage Monday.

High-level summary (tl;dr)
- Prefetch coalescing reduced median tail for long-chat flows (1k+) by ~6–9% p95 on the scrim cluster when used with microbatch size = 6 and kv-cache warming enabled.
- However, enabling aggressive coalescing increased p99 spikes by ~20% under synthetic poisson bursts (50 req/s). Root cause: reordering + head-of-line blocking in the microkernel queue.
- A quick kernel-side fix (lightweight yield after 2 coalesced ops) reduced p99 back to baseline in synthetic tests but needs a more robust scheduling policy to avoid fairness regressions.

What we ran this week
- Monday: baseline capture (no prefetch). Workload: long-chat simulation (avg 900 tokens, 2.2s median service time per request). Metrics captured: token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, KV hit ratio, batch size distribution.
- Tuesday: turned on prefix prefetch + conservative coalesce (delay=6ms, max_coalesce=3). Observed: KV hit ratio +17%, GPU efficiency +11%, end-to-end p95 down 6%. Slack thread: #kernels-prefetch.
- Wednesday: stress test (poisson, mean 50 rps) with aggressive coalesce (delay=20ms, max_coalesce=8). Observed p99 spikes +20%. Captured kernel traces and reordered queue snapshots.
- Thursday: rapid kernel patch (PR 1127) to insert cooperative yielding in the kernel scheduler after 2 back-to-back coalesced tasks. Re-ran stress test: p99 back near baseline, p95 benefit mostly retained.
- Friday: ran mixed tenant test (hosted-mode scaled mix of short-chat / long-chat). Prefetch helped long-chat but increased latency for >95th percentile short-chat requests in some buckets.

Notes from standups and huddles
- Marco: "We need a fairness knob exposed to the runtime API — operators should be able to prioritize short flows during spikes."
- Liang: "Kernel yield is a bandaid; we should look into a queue sharding approach keyed by flow-length estimate."
- Samira (SRE): "Observed an amortized tail when coalescing across tenants with different SLOs; created JIRA-RT-6193 to track isolation mitigations."
- Noah: "Cost numbers look promising if we can keep p99 in check — rough calc shows 8% GPU-token cost reduction for long-chat heavy customers."

Selected data points (from scrim cluster runs)
- Baseline (Mon): p95=420ms, p99=810ms, KV hit=12%, avg batch=3.1
- Conservative coalesce (Tue): p95=395ms, p99=830ms, KV hit=29%, avg batch=4.0
- Aggressive coalesce (Wed): p95=380ms, p99=980ms, KV hit=44%, avg batch=6.8
- Kernel-yield patch (Thu): p95=388ms, p99=820ms, KV hit=43%, avg batch=6.6

Observations / hypotheses
- Hypothesis A: p99 spikes are driven by head-of-line blocking where a large coalesced microbatch stalls while a short request waits behind it.
- Hypothesis B: tenant mixing amplifies the fairness problem — lightweight flows hit higher latency when prefilling warms GPU but then waits behind large prefill ops.
- Hypothesis C: KV warmup is beneficial but currently lacks per-tenant weight; caching policy should account for request priority and token horizon rather than just recency.

Open questions and tests to run
- Q1: Can we implement request-priority preemption in the microkernel queue? Quick experiment: allow short flows (estimated <200 tokens) to short-circuit coalesced ops.
- Q2: Is there a simpler heuristic than full sharding? E.g., maintain two sub-queues (short vs long) with admission ratio tunable by deployment.
- Q3: What's the operational surface for exposing coalescing knobs? Which knobs are safe for customers to fiddle with vs. platform-only?

Action items & owners
- Marco: prototype two-subqueue scheduler and run A/B in scrim by 2027-09-13 (ticket GH#proto-2q).
- Liang: dig into trace logs and produce flamegraphs for p99 cases; focus on reordering metrics (due 2027-09-10).
- Samira: create a runbook note for SRE on how to rollback coalescing knobs in production and add an alert for p99 regression (JIRA-RT-6193 assign).
- Aisha: consolidate cost model estimates for long-chat customers with new KV hit ratios and push to Confluence RT-3421 (due 2027-09-14).
- Noah: run limited canary with two enterprise tenants next week, one with prefetch-enabled and one off (coordinate with customer-success).

Risks and mitigation notes
- Risk: exposing too many knobs increases support burden and misconfigs may cause p99 regressions. Mitigation: platform exposes conservative defaults + feature flags rollouts.
- Risk: kernel changes might mask underlying queue-level fairness issues. Mitigation: pair small kernel fixes with microbenchmarks and end-to-end mixed tenant tests.

Brainstormed alternatives (short)
- Admission control based on flow-length estimator sampled from the first token(s).
- Soft time-slicing inside coalesced batches: if a coalesced batch waits >X ms, preempt and schedule a short flow.
- Per-tenant prefill budget that limits how much a given tenant can warm the KV cache in a window.

Random notes / raw snippets (notes-to-self style)
- saw unusual slow start on one host (i-0a9c) Monday — possible NUMA artifact, re-run isolate.
- consider metric: "prefetch-borne-wasted-ops" = number of prefetches that didn't get used within 10s. Could track for cost accounting.
- Slack: pinged @infra-alloc to check if burst capacity was throttled during Wed stress; they responded that autoscaler briefly clamped GPUs 09:14 UTC.

Next sync
- Quick sync Wed 2027-09-15 09:30am PT. Bring sharding proto results and p99 flamegraphs.

If anything needs to be added to this diary (missing traces, tickets, or quick wins), append below and tag me in Slack.

-- Aisha
